common_name: Primrose Lady Marigold (AAS-Winning Fully Double Primrose-Yellow)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Primrose Lady, an AAS winner, bears fully double, 3-inch primrose-yellow blooms on 20-inch plants.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Primrose Lady, an All-America Selections winner, bears large, fully double, soft primrose-yellow blooms up to three inches across on sturdy, uniform 20-inch plants, a gentler, paler yellow than the deep golds and oranges typical of many African marigolds. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests, making it a classic vegetable-garden companion. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer and pinch young plants to encourage branching.

common_name: First Lady Marigold (AAS-Winning Sunny Yellow Double Marigold)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; First Lady, an AAS winner, bears sunny yellow double blooms to 3.5 inches across on 20-inch plants.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. First Lady, an All-America Selections winner, bears large, fully double, bright sunny-yellow blooms up to three and a half inches across on sturdy, uniform 20-inch plants, one of the earliest-blooming African marigold cultivars to reach flowering size from seed. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests, making it a classic vegetable-garden companion. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer and pinch young plants to encourage branching.

common_name: Big Duck Gold Marigold (AAS-Winning Huge Golden-Yellow Compact Marigold)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Big Duck Gold, an AAS winner, bears huge 3-inch golden-yellow blooms on compact 15-inch plants.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Big Duck Gold, an All-America Selections winner, bears exceptionally large, three-inch, fully double golden-yellow blooms on a notably compact fifteen-inch plant, an unusual combination of large flower size and short stature among African marigold cultivars. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests, making it a classic vegetable-garden companion. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer and pinch young plants to encourage branching.

common_name: Coco Yellow Marigold (Uniform Compact Bright Yellow African Marigold)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Coco Yellow, part of the Coco African-type series, bears uniform compact plants with bright yellow double blooms.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Coco Yellow, part of the compact, uniform Coco African-type marigold series, bears bright yellow, fully double blooms on a tidy, dwarf plant well suited to edging, containers, and mass bedding where the larger, taller African marigold cultivars would be out of scale. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer.

common_name: Legion of Honor Marigold (Classic Heirloom Single Gold with Maroon Blotch)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Legion of Honor, a classic heirloom known since 1903 as Little Brownie, bears single gold flowers marked with maroon blotches at the base.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Legion of Honor, a classic heirloom French marigold long known also as Little Brownie and grown since 1903, bears simple, single, golden-yellow flowers with a distinctive dark maroon blotch marking the base of each petal, an old-fashioned, less showy bloom form than modern double French marigolds but valued for its heirloom pedigree. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer.

common_name: Queen Sophia Marigold (AAS-Winning Semi-Double Orange-Russet Edged Gold)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Queen Sophia, a 1979 AAS winner and RHS Award of Garden Merit holder, bears semi-double anemone-form blooms in deep orange-russet edged gold.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Queen Sophia, a 1979 All-America Selections winner holding a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit, bears semi-double, anemone-form blooms in a rich, warm orange-russet edged with contrasting gold, a distinctive, richly toned color combination and flower form that has kept it a beloved cultivar for over four decades. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer.

common_name: Bonanza Bolero Marigold (AAS-Winning Irregular Gold-and-Red Crested Marigold)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Bonanza Bolero, a 1999 AAS winner, bears irregular gold-and-red double-crested blooms where no two flowers match, on compact 10-12 inch plants.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Bonanza Bolero, a 1999 All-America Selections winner, bears irregularly patterned gold-and-red double-crested blooms in which no two flowers on the plant look quite alike, a lively, unpredictable variegation unusual among French marigold cultivars, on a compact ten-to-twelve-inch plant. Plant in full sun where the strong scent helps deter garden pests. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer.

common_name: Golden Gem Marigold (Deep Golden-Yellow Signet Marigold with Orange Centers)

planting.note: Start indoors a few weeks before last frost or sow directly once soil warms; Golden Gem, an RHS-listed signet marigold, bears deep golden-yellow flowers with orange centers on a compact, mounding habit.

directions: Start seeds indoors for a head start or sow directly after frost danger passes, barely covering them. Golden Gem, an RHS-listed signet marigold, bears small, single, deep golden-yellow flowers with contrasting orange centers over finely cut, lacy, citrus-scented foliage on a compact, mounding plant, part of the edible-flower Tagetes tenuifolia group prized for both ornamental and culinary use. Plant in full sun; unlike larger African and French marigolds, signet types tolerate light shade and thrive in containers and edging. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer.

Starfire, an heirloom signet marigold seed mix, bears small, single flowers in a lively tricolor blend of yellow, orange, and red-mahogany tones over finely cut, lemon-verbena-scented foliage on a compact, mounding plant, part of the edible-flower Tagetes tenuifolia group prized for both ornamental and culinary use. Plant in full sun; unlike larger African and French marigolds, signet types tolerate light shade and thrive in containers and edging. Deadhead spent blooms to keep flowers coming all summer.
